How It Works

To receive the benefit, sign up for a monthly or annual Uber One membership (subject to auto-renewal, terms apply) through uber.com/uberone and use an eligible Platinum Card® on the Card Account as the form of payment for your membership. Card Members with an existing membership must update their Uber One membership payment method to an eligible Card on the Card Account to receive the benefit. Uber Cash balances must be toggled off for Uber One membership fees to receive the benefit.

Uber One membership charges by both the Basic and Additional Card Members on the Account will receive up to $120 in statement credits each calendar year. However, the Card Account is only eligible for a total of $120 in statement credits per calendar year, per Card Account.

Statement credits are typically received within a few days but may take up to 8 weeks after an eligible purchase is charged to the Card Account.

It’s rather brilliant on Oura’s part. Similar to how HP for many years sold printers that were around the actual cost to manufacture but made the real money selling refill cartridges at huge margins, Oura can sell a lot of these rings at full price (even if they are subsidizing 100% of the $200 credit) to all these people with Platinum cards, many of whom may never have considered (or even heard of) the product and then sell them all a monthly membership that costs Oura next to nothing to provide. Then as the 2nd and 3rd waves of these rings are sold on the secondary market by Platinum holders who already have one for themselves, Oura accumulates additional incremental monthly subscriptions from people who were even less likely to pay full price for the rings to begin with (yet Oura made the initial sale at full price to the Platinum holder, who is the one selling at a discount). They’re basically giving away the low-margin rings at cost–or maybe less–but banking on the continued revenue stream of the high-margin subscriptions.

I have 2 business Platinum cards, and with the refresh I expected to cancel one of them once the next annual fee is due. However, I’ve now used the $300 FHR 2025 credit for both cards, with 2 separate reservations, and I have to say that I find this benefit to be amazing.

I’m usually pretty frugal, though travel is my indulgence. I’m used to traveling on points, which feels like I travel for free. I used the benefit for Conrad Evermore in Orlando, mid-December for a 1 night 36 hour stay. It cost me $150 after the credit (I realize it really cost me somewhere between $150 and $450, including the annual fee and how many benefits I can take advantage of). The stay was amazing. My second trip was last week at Fairmont in San Juan-area. 2 nights, booked last minute for Christmas. Total value was $2,400 with free breakfast, room upgrade, free Cabana and $100 credit. After the $300 back I ended up paying a net of $1,200. At each hotel they also gave some nice gifts like a box of chocolates or a straw logo bag with a logo hat. Very indulgent and well worth it to me. I already max out a lot of the other benefits like the phone and travel credits, so for now these cards are keepers.
FYI Saks 5th is filing for chapter 11. If you’re worried at all, go spend the $50 as soon as possible in the new year
